sources.title: You cannot replay missions in GTA 6, but you can use multiple save files, as Rockstar explains how it made missions "harder to fail"
sources.text: You cannot replay GTA 6 missions again once you've completed them. This might be a shock to some people, since the option to do so was included in Rockstar games as recently as GTA 5 , but here once you've made progress in the story, that's it. Our reviewer confirmed this in his 100+ hour playthrough of the title. You can, of course, use the game's 15 save slots instead - but considering that there will be many, many more missions than there are slots, you're going to have to think about when and where you want to make a record of your progress. By my maths, that means you're going to want to make a new manual save for every 6.6 percent of the game you complete. There is, of course, an auto-save slot, too, that should help you out if you get Busted or Wasted. There will also be key story missions - you will be able to tell when they are, much like you could tell when there was about to be a big heist in GTA 5, a showdown in GTA: San Andreas, or a raid on a gang lord's mansion in GTA: Vice City - that you may want to save before attempting. It seems, though, that it's going to be a bit harder than in previous games to hit that fail state in GTA 6. "The team embraced more of an open-ended design philosophy on this project," says David Hynd, vice president of technology on GTA 6. "For example, we really wanted to reduce the number of Mission fails for the player experimenting or trying something different. And we wanted to encourage the player to do what felt right to them for their particular play style." That means that Rockstar, by considering its deployment of standard gameplay mechanics and enemy AI, and re-evaluating how it approached mission and level design, has created "many different ways" for you to approach any given mission in the game. The result? "It's a lot harder to keep Missions as open as possible (especially in a game as large as this), but the freedom and flexibility it allows the player was worth it," says Hynd. He also notes that the team expects players to "learn and reapply" consistent rules in terms of how the world works - and be surprised when they do and don't apply. In the previous game, you could access any previous mission you'd completed and be able to play it again on a whim. For GTA 5, you'd simply boot up Story Mode, open the pause menu, go to Game > Replay Mission, and pick the mission you want to play. GTA 6's structure is more complicated, though, hence why Rockstar made the decision to make progress this linear. GTA 6 comes out tomorrow. You can find a breakdown of all the global launch times for GTA 6 at the link, and read our 5-star review of the game here . If you want to, ahem, 'travel to New Zealand' to get ahead of the timezones, it seems the country would be happy to have you .

sources.title: Just how detailed is the audio in GTA 6? Well, even convenience store refrigerators "all have their own unique sounds", says Rockstar dev
sources.text: If you've been online at all today, you'll know that what feels like the entire world is currently fawning over GTA 6. As the reviews dropped , one thing quickly became very clear: this is a game absolutely packed with detail. Our own Chris noted that, thanks to this focus on specific detail and unbelievable nuance, Grand Theft Auto 6 is "the most unbelievable video game world ever made". And it's no accident: this is something Rockstar put a lot of dedicated effort into. It's been well-established that the studio has gone above and beyond to make this interactive world one of the most richly-developed we've ever seen: Rockstar has told us it "re-engineered" its weather systems to "achieve a sense of scale we haven't felt before," adding hurricanes, rainbows and heavy rain . It simulated and built a complex drug system, allowing Lucia and Jason to partake in drug use "directly from their inventory" and "at any time" . But there are still details emerging from the dev team that are blowing my mind. And the most recent byte of information I saw was related to how Rockstar worked with sound. "Much of the dynamic soundscape is informed by the incredibly detailed art throughout the world," explains Alastair MacGregor, vice president of audio at Rockstar. "One small example is that convenience store refrigerators all have their own unique sounds. In a run-down store, the refrigerators and freezers are loud and sound like they are badly maintained. Their compressor units can be heard mechanically whirring away from years of neglect. As a result, the bottles behind the doors can be heard shaking and the units click on and off more frequently. In an up-market store, the refrigerators are quieter, adding a subtle hum to the environment." This level of detail is, quite frankly, absurd. It's a testament to granularity Rockstar is willing to go to in making Leonida feel truly lived-in and realistic. And this level of production isn't restricted to internal locations, either. "On the ambient side, we love the contrast between the manicured luxury islands, with the sizzle of crickets and lawn sprinklers backed by birdsong, yacht halyards clanging in the distance, and yard work going on, versus urban areas with the sounds of people living on top of each other - snatches of every genre of music, distant voices, cars peeling out, construction, the omnipresent hum of elderly air conditioners struggling with the humidity," continues MacGregor. He goes on to say that if you're wandering the streets of Gellhorn - a coastal city in Kelly County on the western side of Leonida - it's acoustically a very different vibe than the high-rise centre of Vice City, where the sound bounces between the buildings. This means that the engine is handling not just the sounds of things as minute as bugs in the grass, but also how that sound travels, and interacts with other physical entities in the world. "We've spent years iterating on reverb technology to make sure that you can feel that - from the pops of cars backfiring to the wash of a helicopter passing by overhead to birds squawking in the trees," concludes MacGregor. GTA 6 launches tomorrow - Thursday, 19th November - for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It's also worth noting that Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees . The case's conclusion will be determined this week .

sources.title: 'We need to come together': On the eve of GTA 6, 1,600 Rockstar workers are voting on unionization
sources.text: "Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too." As I write this, reviews for Grand Theft Auto 6 have gone live. Gamers in New Zealand have been able to play it for almost six hours, and millions of people farther west are eagerly waiting for clocks to hit midnight in their own timezones. In preorder sales alone, GTA 6 has already generated over $1.6 billion in revenue , and will undoubtedly earn millions more over its launch weekend. As Rockstar is poised to set historic records with its latest release, the workers who made it could be making history of its own: Over 1,600 Rockstar employees in the UK are currently voting on whether to form a union. If it wins recognition when the ballot closes on November 26, the Rockstar Games Workers Union would be the largest in the UK games sector, organizing workers at what's arguably the games industry's highest-profile studio—a major milestone in the push for unionization in game development. In an op-ed for The Guardian , Rockstar animation programmer and union representative Nestor Uriarte said the studio's possible unionization is the product of a decade-long realization that "to tackle the industry's mounting challenges we need to come together." Union recognition, he said, would help safeguard the working conditions of the developers who built GTA 6 into an already record-breaking success. "Behind these numbers are thousands of people whose talent and hard work make the games possible. With a recognized union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to," Uriarte said. "Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too." Working conditions at Rockstar produced one of the early flashpoints in the advancing push for games industry unionization over recent years, sparked by employees' descriptions of its "death march" crunch culture and allegations of sexual assault . While the studio's taken steps towards a healthier workplace in the years since, employees have reported continuing concerns around gender pay gaps, crunch, and nebulous bonuses conditions. Coinciding with the union vote, a Glasgow tribunal is weighing testimonies in the ongoing legal battle around Rockstar's alleged union-busting and firing of employees who had been involved in organization. Meanwhile, just days before a launch that's projected to earn landmark revenue, Rockstar parent company 2K reportedly laid off a third of the employees at XCOM and Civilization developer Firaxis. "It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off," Uriarte said. "But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised." From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews Union recognition, he said, would also provide developers with a greater ability to negotiate the rapid proliferation of AI in game development, which represents yet another threat of worker devaluation in an industry where one third of the labor force has been laid off in the last two years. A Rockstar union would help protect its workers' future—and the future of the studio. "We’ve heard from colleagues who are nervous that the union is an outside troublemaking force that will threaten the company," Uriarte said. "But we’re not outsiders. We are hundreds of studio employees who live for Rockstar, its output, and the players. We want to see it succeed." sources.title: Crimson Desert snubs at The Game Awards are "a terrible shame," Palworld lead says
sources.text: Crimson Desert was only nominated for one award The nominees have been revealed for The Game Awards 2026, and Palworld lead John "Bucky" Buckley is amongst those disappointed that Crimson Desert is up for just one award – and it's not Game of the Year. This year's GOTY nominees are an interesting bunch, not least because GTA 6 is one of the options – announced yesterday, before the game's launch and even before the GTA 6 reviews went live. Joining Rockstar's game in the running are The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Resident Evil Requiem, Control: Resonant, 007 First Light, and Phantom Blade Zero. Notably, no Crimson Desert. In fact, the only category Pearl Abyss's game has been nominated for is Best Community Support – no doubt a result of the devs' constant updates that have added improvements and new features since launch. But alas, Pocketpair's head of publishing and communications isn't best pleased. "To nominate Crimson Desert for nothing other than best community support? Not even best RPG or best adventure?" he asks. "To say I'm disappointed would be an understatement. What a shame. What a terrible shame." And he's not the only one. Following the nomination announcements, many Crimson Desert fans took to social media to express their disappointment. "The disrespect is insane. GTA 6 should not be on this list. WHERE THE FUCK IS CRIMSON DESERT!?" one responds , looking at the selection of GOTY nominees. "Crimson Desert Wins PC Game of the Year at the Joystick Awards and doesn't get a GOTY nomination at The Game Awards... The amount of disrespect this game has and continues to get is insane," says another , as another writes : "The lack of nominations in either the Best RPG or Best Action/Adventure categories is genuinely baffling." Bucky's response here is no surprise – he's been championing Crimson Desert since its launch earlier this year, recently calling it "one of the most technically ambitious games we've seen in the last decade" but one that's "underrated" since it "isn't another linear narrative RPG with the illusion of freedom." Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more There's always discourse around events like The Game Awards as, inevitably, we all have our favorites. Crimson Desert isn't the only big 2026 game to receive a low number of nominations, either – Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, for example, also got just the one in Best Role Playing Game, along with Final Fantasy Resonance. Despite Crimson Desert's AI backlash, Pearl Abyss is now implementing the tech "throughout our entire development pipeline" – including for upcoming Pokemon-like DokeV. sources.title: Rockstar President Sam Houser Issues Rare Statement to Celebrate GTA 6 Launch
sources.text: As GTA 6 launches around the world, Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser has issued a rare statement to celebrate the occasion and "many more years" of experiences ahead. While other high-ranking Rockstar staff have discussed GTA 6 in interviews thus far, the famously reclusive producer has now outlined his company's intentions with the game, and suggested there was much more to come in future. "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with all of us," Houser began, in a statement shared with IGN's GTA 6 reviewer, Luke Reilly . "This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special. "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world full of possibilities — and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes. "We hope it felt both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope that you had fun. We are incredibly grateful to you and everything that you do to celebrate games. We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you. While Houser's rare statement is notable enough on its own, the mention of "many more years" of experiences from Rockstar will inevitably excite fans already wondering what's next from the company. While the base GTA 6 offers hundreds of hours of experiences to discover and enjoy, there is of course huge speculation surrounding the game's unannounced but inevitable online portion. As of yet, Rockstar has not discussed its next iteration of GTA Online at all, though fans expect to hear something of it sooner or later. The current GTA 5 version of GTA Online has raked in around $5 billion so far since its arrival back in 2013. sources.title: As GTA 6 finally releases, Rockstar boss Sam Houser issues rare statement
sources.text: "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling" GTA 6 is finally here. The long-awaited sequel arrives 13 years after the release of GTA 5 for PS3 and Xbox 360. It's a moment worth celebrating. Clearly, Rockstar Games feels the same way, as the studio's elusive co-founder and president makes a rare statement to help welcome you to Leonida. "Rockstar Games was founded on the belief that games could achieve the same distinction as all other forms of storytelling, become essential to modern culture, and to be thought of as stories and worlds that live on with us," says Houser, in a comment released to GamesRadar+. "This week, Grand Theft Auto returns to Leonida and modern-day Vice City. While things have changed and time has passed, one aspect holds true: We have tried to create an experience that will exceed your expectations while showing what this medium is capable of, and why we believe games are so special." Houser has an executive producer credit on every mainline installment of the Grand Theft Auto series, and has served as a central creative lead and source of truth within the studio. He knows better than most just how important Rockstar's sprawling virtual worlds are to players, and the breadth of interest this return to Vice City will attract around the world. It's a challenge he doesn't take lightly. "Whether you can trace your journey to this game through the entire series or are experiencing Grand Theft Auto for the first time, this is a narrative set in a world of possibilities – and it is up to you as the player to shape how it ultimately feels, and concludes. We hope it feels both familiar and entirely new, and above all, we hope you have fun." Houser's statement concludes: "We look forward to many more years of sharing these experiences with you." Many more years is right. While Grand Theft Auto 6 has launched as a single-player-only experience (and the studio is yet to officially comment on whether a successor to GTA Online is in development), I can say from my own personal experience with the game that it presents the sort of reactive world which will have the capacity to surprise and delight for years to come. sources.text: Plus what happens when you reach the new highest heat level. Achieving six stars in GTA 6 's new wanted system is the most notoriety you can get in the game, and killing enough cops and soldiers to get there will likely have a big impact on your criminal profile —which is effectively this game's version of Red Dead Redemption 2's karma system. As with the previous games, the highest star levels are reserved for trespassing in an airport and stealing a passenger jet, or heading to a military base and hijacking an APC. And, as always, five stars will see a tank dispatched. But you can only get to six stars if you cause mass destruction and loss of life. The only way we were able to get a six star wanted level in GTA 6 was by stealing a tank from a military base and blowing up other tanks and vehicles. You can run but you can't hide because once you're at six stars, the law will never stop hunting you. This means your only way out is to die, essentially. It's also worth considering that killing all of those cops could impact your criminal profile quite severely. sources.title: How to clone keys in GTA 6
sources.text: Trouble stealing a car? There's an app for that. Vice City's glow-up in GTA 6 ushers in a new era of smart car tech, bringing keyless ignition to the series. That's great for car owners, but a pain for our criminal duo since you can't hotwire a keyless car. Luckily, that doesn't mean you can't steal a car with high-tech security. Modern problems call for modern crimes, and that's where the key cloner comes in. Standard trackers on stolen cars aren't much of a problem—they just forbid you from making modifications at a mod shop unless you register the car as your own. Advanced trackers , however, are a whole other beast. They relay your exact location to the cops, but you can outrun the signal if you're fast enough. Keep your foot on the gas, and the cops won't be able to track you until you slow down. Apparently, the solution to beat high-tech surveillance is still a good ol' fashioned pedal-to-the-metal joyride. sources.text: Calame , a single-player isometric strategy RPG that “blends deep, classic strategy with innovative reality-shifting gameplay,” will launch for PlayStation 5 , Xbox Series , and PC via Steam in February 2027, developer Nextale Games announced. A demo is currently available for PC. Here is an overview of the game, via Nextale: In the Shadow of the King of Light, History is Written by the Survivors In Westalia, renown is more than just a story—it is a weapon of mass destruction. When belief in a legend grows strong enough, it can physically reshape the battlefield or devour those who wield it. To overthrow the tyrannical King of Light, the Rebellion must learn to harness this divine force without becoming the very monsters they fight. But how do you save a kingdom when you are tearing yourselves apart? An uneasy alliance forms the core of the Rebellion. On one side, Kenmare fights for the freedom of the people; on the other, the Panthers fight to reclaim the throne. While their alliance is a matter of sheer survival, their visions for the future are utterly irreconcilable—and you are the one chosen to lead them. A New Kind of Tactics That Rewrites the Battlefield Itself In the finest tradition of genre classics, Calame delivers demanding, handcrafted, grid-based combat where positioning, unit facing and class synergies are the keys to survival. Players can customize their army utilizing a diverse roster of melee specialists, ranged fighters, mages and support classes to trigger devastating party combinations. However, Calame breaks the tactical mold with its groundbreaking “Correction” feature—an innovative new strategy mechanic allowing you to rewrite and manipulate the battlefield mid-combat, turning the terrain itself into a dynamic weapon! Beyond the battlefield, Calame features deep progression systems including RPG leveling, skill unlocks, and legendary gear collection. Your journey is heavily defined by a reactive choice system. Decisions made at camp and during narrative events directly alter the Rebellion’s political alignment, unlocking powerful passive traits that permanently reshape your squad’s playstyle, faction relationships and the unfolding story.
